extracted.intended_audience: screenwriters, filmmakers, festival programmers, and prospective festival attendees/submission authors
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Austin Film Festival's programs, competitions, awards, and conference with an emphasis on screenwriting, screenplay/teleplay submission categories, judging, and writer-focused educational outreach. Useful for writers considering submission or attendance and for understanding what the festival values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on writers' creative contributions to film
rubrics_metrics.description: Austin Film Festival (AFF) is an organization that focuses on writers' creative contributions to film. Initially called the Austin Heart of Film Screenwriters Conference, it functioned to launch the careers of screenwriters, who historically have been underrepresented within the film industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival emphasizes the role of screenplays in filmmaking and programs events (panels, conversations, workshops) that celebrate and teach craft; selection and programming are oriented toward writing and writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showcase the art and craft of strong narrative storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each October, Austin Film Festival & Conference presents a program of narrative, animated and documentary features and shorts. Films showcase the art and craft of strong narrative storytelling and screenings are often accompanied by question and answer sessions with cast members and filmmakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming favors films that exemplify strong narrative storytelling; Q&A and panel contexts foreground story and craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenplay Competition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories for the Screenplay Competition include: Drama; Comedy; The Enderby Entertainment Award; The Skybound Entertainment Sci-Fi Award; Horror; The HUMANITAS Originals; Short Screenplay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must select the appropriate category; the festival also added Playwriting and Scripted Fiction Podcast competitions and accepts Scripted Digital Series (both written and produced), broadening submission formats the festival supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleplay Competition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories for the Teleplay Competition include: AMC One-Hour Pilot; One-Hour Spec; Sitcom Pilot; Sitcom Spec; The HUMANITAS Originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teleplay entrants should choose the appropriate category reflecting format and hour/spec status; the festival also recognizes scripted digital series formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process for screenplay and teleplay competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1994, Austin Film Festival has been recognizing writers through the Screenplay and Teleplay Competitions. With representatives from agencies and production companies participating in the judging process, advancing writers and their scripts gain industry attention, networking opportunities and workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges have included representatives from Warner Bros., Nickelodeon Movies, ABC Studios, Pixar, United Talent Agency, and others — indicating industry-oriented evaluation criteria (commercial/readiness, craft, voice, market fit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalist advancement benefits and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: All awards are presented during the Austin Film Festival Awards Luncheon. Those advancing to the Semifinalist level or beyond will have the option to attend exclusive panels hosted by participating panelists. Finalists in all categories receive one complimentary Producer's Badge to attend the Austin Film Festival and Conference and one complimentary Awards Luncheon ticket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advancement confers industry exposure (Producers Book distribution, access to panels, networking) and tangible attendance privileges intended to help writers market their work and meet industry professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenings selection emphasis: premieres and independent films
rubrics_metrics.description: The festival programs include premieres, advance screenings and independent films, often featuring world and U.S. premieres in the film slate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmers (named in past years) curate lineups with a bias toward premieres and independent films that highlight storytelling and emerging talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMPAS accreditation and short film award eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: AFF is accredited by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences, making all Jury Award-winning Narrative Short, Documentary Short, and Animated Short films eligible for an Academy Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jury Award-winning shorts at AFF gain eligibility for Oscar consideration — a selection criterion that can raise the stakes and visibility for short-film submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference session topics and craft emphases
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference features panels, conversations, workshops, roundtables, script-to-screen examples, and sessions covering basics like researching and editing your story, pitching and marketing your script or film, finding and working with a writing partner or director, facing a blank page on a bad day, or risking a new direction after establishing success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sessions include in-depth script-to-screen presentations and conversations with established writers/filmmakers; practical craft and career-development topics indicate what skills and behaviors the festival promotes among writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and recognition categories for contributors to industry
rubrics_metrics.description: AFF has multiple awards recognizing industry contributions: Distinguished Screenwriter Award; Outstanding Television Writer Award; Extraordinary Contribution to Filmmaking Award; Extraordinary Contribution to Film - Acting Award; Heart of Film Award; Polly Platt Award for Producing; New Voice Award; Writers’ Writer Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These awards signal the festival's evaluative priorities — honoring established craft, television writing, filmmaking contributions, producing, emerging/new voices, and peer-recognized writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Young Filmmakers Program and Digital Storytelling education standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Young Filmmakers Program (ages 9–18) and Digital Storytelling (DS) arts-education program improve students' reading, writing and communication skills using film. DS provides curriculum, reading materials, equipment, and professional filmmaker instructors and has been integrated into high school English Language Arts with TEKS alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational program success is measured by literacy/test-prep outcomes (example: Akins High School TEKS score increases), access via scholarships (300+), and curricular integration; shows AFF values pedagogical alignment and measurable learning outcomes in outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record / outcomes for competition participants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Screenplay Competition receives more entries than any other competition in the world; several competition finalists and semi-finalists have made sales or found managers and agents at the conference. Past winners and participants (e.g., Jason Reitman, Cary Fukanaga) have gone on to significant industry success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival advancement and awards are framed as indicators of industry-readiness and career-launch potential; historical pickups (films picked up for distribution, Academy nominations/wins) are cited as outcomes supporting the festival's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: On Story series as an extension of festival craft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: On Story, AFF's television series, presents footage from AFF panels and screenings featuring screenwriters and filmmakers discussing their talents and films, airing episodes with one or two short films previously screened at the Festival and introductions from the film's writer or director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Story distributes craft-focused conversations to a wider audience and publishes consolidated advice (book publication), reinforcing the festival's role as a source of practical screenwriting guidance and examples.
